title: Text Mining and Information Extraction from Croatian Military Publications: A Longitudinal Study of Hrvatski vojnik (1991–2026)
content: The increasing availability of digital military publications offers opportunities to investigate how defense institutions, capabilities, and international cooperation are represented over time. This study applies text-mining and information-extraction methods to Hrvatski vojnik (‘Croatian Soldier’), a Croatian military journal, to identify prominent terminology, thematic patterns, and named entities. The dataset comprises 231 of 920 recorded journal entries (1991–2026), selected by year-stratified random sampling. The workflow included OCR-based text conversion, preprocessing, keyword and word-frequency analysis, temporal comparison, Latent Semantic Indexing (LSI), Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA), extractive summarization, and named entity recognition with the Croatian spaCy model. Frequent terms concerned Croatia, the armed forces, military capabilities, and defense structures, alongside equipment-specific vocabulary. General vocabulary remained stable across four publication periods, while content terms followed the editorial profile of each period: vojni (‘military’) nearly doubled after the 1990s, hrvatski (‘Croatian’) fell in 2000–2009 and peaked in 2020–2026, and brod (‘ship’) declined steadily, and sustav (‘system’) fell until 2010–2019 and then rose slightly. Organizations formed the largest category of named entities. The study demonstrates the practical potential of these methods for exploring military publications, while highlighting challenges in text extraction, linguistic processing, and entity normalization, and provides an exploratory basis for further computational analysis of Croatian military discourse.
